harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured centralized syslog forwarding from node2 (inventory app, identified by [REDACTED] programname "inventory") to node1 using Ansible run from the control node (node3). node1 runs rsyslog with imudp/imtcp listeners on port 514 bound to a dedicated ruleset that writes matching messages to /var/log/inventory/node2.log; node2 forwards messages tagged "inventory" to node1:514/tcp via a disk-assisted omfwd queue for resiliency. rsyslog is enabled+started on both nodes so the pipeline survives reboots. Verified log delivery before and after restarting node2, node1, and node3 (control node) one at a time, confirming boot-id changes and full recovery of the flow after each restart.
actions_performed: Surveyed all 3 nodes: confirmed no pre-existing 'inventory' app/service, node3 is the ansible-controller (control_node), node1/node2 are vanilla Ubuntu 24.04 with rsyslog installed but ssh.service failed (missing host keys)
Regenerated SSH host keys and started ssh on node1/node2 to enable Ansible connectivity
Set up passwordless SSH from node3 to node1/node2 using CLUSTER_SSH_PRIVKEY/PUBKEY

Wrote an Ansible inventory (collector=node1, app=node2) and a 3-play playbook: (1) ensure rsyslog installed/enabled/started on all hosts, (2) on node1 create /var/log/inventory dir and deploy a collector ruleset (imudp+imtcp on 514, filtering fromhost-ip==node2 and programname==inventory into node2.log), (3) on node2 deploy a forwarding rule (omfwd over TCP to node1:514 with a disk-assisted queue) for programname==inventory, each with a restart-rsyslog handler
Ran ansible-playbook from node3 successfully (all tasks ok/changed as expected)
Verified end-to-end: logger -t inventory on node2 appeared in /var/log/inventory/node2.log on node1
Captured pre-restart boot-id baselines on node1, node2, node3
Restarted node2, then node1, then node3 one at a time via native reboot; polled each until exec was available again and confirmed boot-id changed
After each restart, verified rsyslog active/enabled and re-tested log delivery end-to-end (5 sequential test messages all persisted correctly across all 3 restarts)

evidence.requirement: Ansible playbook configures log forwarding from node2 to node1
evidence.summary: ansible ping succeeded to node1/node2, then ansible-playbook run completed with all tasks ok/changed and no failures
rsyslog listening on 0.0.0.0:514 tcp/udp on node1; logger -t inventory on node2 produced a matching line in /var/log/inventory/node2.log

evidence.requirement: Log flow keeps working after node2 restart
evidence.summary: Baseline boot-id c0691b74... captured, reboot triggered (connection timed out confirms disruption), post-reboot boot-id bde232b6... (changed), rsyslog active/enabled, new logger message appended to node1's node2.log

evidence.requirement: Log flow keeps working after node1 restart
evidence.summary: Baseline boot-id 29011044... captured earlier, reboot triggered (timeout confirms disruption), post-reboot boot-id 0bcb3c7a... (changed), rsyslog active/enabled and listening on 514 again, node2.log directory/file intact, new logger message from node2 appended successfully

Baseline boot-id d5f5239f... captured, reboot triggered (connection errors confirm disruption), post-reboot boot-id 7c6e36c1... (changed), ansible/ansible-playbook present and SSH to node2 working again post-reboot

evidence.requirement: Final full-system verification after all 3 nodes restarted
evidence.summary: logger test message from node2 sent after all three nodes were rebooted; node1's /var/log/inventory/node2.log shows all 5 cumulative test messages including the final one, proving the forwarding pipeline survived every restart
